title: IvyLoop SaaS Onramp - integration scratchbook
body:
Call notes (2025-01-14)
Participants: Daniel (Redwood), Maya (SE), Sofia (Redwood PM), Evan Li (IvyLoop Eng), Priya Kapoor (IvyLoop Security)

High-level ask:
- IvyLoop wants a customer-hosted inference integration inside a VPC (private deployment) for their returns assistant. Must satisfy GDPR + FedRAMP-adjacent controls (audit logs, KMS).
- Target latency: 95th <= 180ms per token for short responses (<=256 tokens), target p95 end-to-end 400ms for single-turn summarization workflow. Peak throughput: ~300 rps sustained for 2-hour trading window, typical steady-state 60–80 rps.
- Session model: conversational threads pinned to an affinity key, KV cache reuse per customer-session recommended.

Immediate technical constraints mentioned by IvyLoop:
- All inference must remain inside their AWS account VPC (no egress without approved CIDR).
- Use their KMS for model keys and secrets, HSM optional.
- Network: they have transit gateway + private subnet with existing NAT disabled; need to confirm route tables for control plane telemetry.
- Data residency: EU-first, primary region eu-west-1 with fallback to us-east-1.

Model/quality constraints:
- They prefer open models; want Redwood to validate a 7B/13B mix (fast path for quick replies, 13B for longer summarization).
- Concern about hallucination on invoice parsing — require a small eval set (50 representative examples) to track regressions post-rollout.

Operational gotchas called out during call (raw):
- Cold-start latency on warmup after autoscale (they have spiky ingestion) — want warm pool strategy (reserved capacity) or pre-warm hooks.
- Token accounting: their finance team wants per-session cost estimates; need Redwood token-level breakdown exported daily to S3 (CSV).
- Prefix caching: many sessions reuse last 3 messages; confirm how Redwood's KV caching applies across model variants (7B vs 13B) and quantized kernels.
- Canary rollouts must support fast rollback to previous pinned model. They asked specifically about A/B traffic split at routing layer.

Integration specifics / engineering notes:
- Proposed network setup: private-deploy with customer control plane (Redwood Private). We'll run inference plane in their VPC using customer-managed ENIs. Control plane will be limited to outbound https on egress-allowed IP ranges.
- Auth: use IAM-based cert exchange + short-lived tokens from Redwood connector. Must support their security policy "no long-lived secrets in S3".
- Metrics: need Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoints or push gateway. They requested application-level metrics: tokens/sec, avg-latency/token, kv-cache-hit-rate, model-version.

Experiment ideas (to discuss with research):
- Mixed-precision quant profiles: 4-bit quant for 7B for cost savings, 8-bit for 13B. Measure impact on hallucination on the 50-eval set.
- Hybrid routing: route short queries to 7B with prefix caching, long summaries to 13B via smart routing; use latency budget to decide fallback.

Open questions (to resolve before scoping):
- Q1: Can IvyLoop expose a private endpoint for Redwood control plane egress? If not, what audit payloads are acceptable to send off-VPC?
- Q2: Confirm peak concurrent KV cache size expectations (Evan to provide histogram of average conversation lengths and unique prefixes).
- Q3: Which S3 bucket will receive daily billing exports and do they require encryption-only SSE-KMS with their key?
- Q4: Acceptable RTO for upgrades and rollbacks (they suggested max 5 minutes for emergency rollback).

Action items / next steps (owners + ETA):
- Evan (IvyLoop): send conversation length histogram + sample messages (anonymized) by 2025-01-21. (blocked: legal review)
- Daniel (Redwood): produce a one-page network diagram proposal + list of egress IPs for control-plane by 2025-01-17.
- Maya (Redwood SE): run a quick local eval comparing 7B-quant vs 7B-fp16 on their invoice eval set; share results by 2025-01-24.
- Sofia (Redwood PM): draft initial SOW estimate for Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private deployment options, include cost delta and latency expectations; deliver draft 2025-01-28.
- Priya (IvyLoop Security): confirm KMS key policy and whether HSM primitives required by 2025-01-22.

Risks & mitigation notes:
- Risk: If NAT/route restrictions prevent control plane telemetry, we may need a sidecar for local telemetry buffering and periodic push to customer-managed S3. Mitigation: design a push-only agent that lives in their subnet.
- Risk: Quantization regression causing accuracy drop on invoice extraction. Mitigation: hold final model behind canary with automatic rollback if eval metrics drop >2% F1.

Meeting follow-up plan:
- 30-min technical deep-dive scheduled 2025-01-20 (Evan + Priya + Daniel + Maya). Goal: finalize network setup and telemetry agreement.
- Share a short README in Confluence with links to sample request/response shapes, required IAM roles, and example terraform snippets for connector deployment.

Random scratch ideas captured in call (not committed):
- Warm KV priming: replay top-50 prefixes during expected spikes to reduce cold token cost.
- Token-level billing preview: small lambda to simulate monthly cost from sampled traffic for finance.

Notes to self (Daniel):
- Call felt security-heavy — prioritize network + KMS answers in follow-up.
- Keep SOW neutral: show both Dedicated and Private options with clear tradeoffs.
- Add a short demo script for canary rollback during deep-dive.

End of scratchbook entry.
